To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a feature space of 104 dimensions may be used in a content-based image retrieval system, provided that the query is restricted to the subspace defined by the features present; (ii) the use of an index based on an inverted file data structures is a practical and efficient means of implementing the subspace restriction, and of performing the feature weighting; and (iii) relevance feedback improves the performance of a content-based image query system.
the use of an appropriate feature set, an efficient inverted file structure, and relevance feedback, can result in good performance in a content-based retrieval system.

(1) the use of an index of features permits the efficient search of high dimensional feature spaces; (2) the use of relevance feedback queries improves system performance; and (3) colour and texture features can be combined in a single query, with no significant loss of performance, and with the added benefit of improved user interface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a content-based retrieval system that is capable of dealing with the high-dimensional feature spaces that characterise the image domain.
the development of a system for content-based image query which combines the advantages of the vector space model of text retrieval with the use of colour and texture as features.
the use of techniques from text retrieval to improve the performance of content-based image retrieval systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of an appropriate feature set in a suitably weighted inverted file data structure provides a simple and effective approach to content-based image retrieval.

the use of an index structure based on a weighted feature vector representation is a powerful tool, and that the use of a relevance feedback mechanism is an effective means of improving system performance.

the use of a sparse feature set and an inverted file representation of the feature space is a promising approach for content-based query of large collections of images, and that relevance feedback is a useful means of improving system performance in such an environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how a text retrieval framework, combined with an inverted file data representation, is a viable approach to content-based query of images.

the use of an efficient data structure, together with the use of a small number of features, and an appropriate weighting scheme, allows a content-based query system to be built which is both efficient, and effective.

we have demonstrated that a simple, low cost, and effective content-based image retrieval system is possible, and that this is achievable by applying techniques that have been developed in the context of text retrieval.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by combining the use of an index structure with the use of a small, sparse feature set and the use of relevance feedback, it is possible to obtain good results from the content-based retrieval of images using a single query, without the need for complex and expensive learning techniques.
the use of an index structure based on the features present in a collection permits the use of large feature spaces, and the use of relevance feedback to improve performance.
the use of an efficient data structure, and the use of a sparse set of features, permits the use of large feature spaces in content-based image retrieval systems.
